title: Structured lifecycle matrix and staged upgrade orchestration for runtime, API, SDKs, and console
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a single, actionable LTS support matrix across the four product surfaces (serving runtime, Redwood API, official SDKs, Redwood Console) and design the staged rollout and upgrade orchestration. Deliverables: a published matrix, gating rules for automated rollouts (canary -> ramp -> full), and a set of upgrade automation primitives (migration CLI, health-check hooks, rollback playbooks).
acceptance_criteria: Published LTS support matrix doc that maps runtime builds to API versions and SDK minor versions
Automated rollout pipeline implemented in CI that supports canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% stages with metric-based gates
Upgrade tooling prototype (redwood-upgrade CLI) that performs dry-run, migration steps, and automated rollback on failure
Compatibility policy enforced in the release CI: incompatible changes must be flagged and require explicit opt-in
Console UI displays per-tenant supported version and recommended upgrade path
notes: Work stems from multiple incidents where customers pinned older runtime binaries while SDKs advanced leading to subtle API surface regressions. The goal is to make LTS a predictable contract: minor SDK updates remain compatible within an LTS channel; runtime ABI changes require a new LTS line. We're coordinating with SDK, runtime, and console squads to produce a single source of truth.
decision_log: 2026-03-11 - Adopt semver-like channel labels: stable (rolling) / lts-v1 / lts-v2. Channels map to concrete runtime build series and API compatibility guarantees.
2026-03-12 - Gate thresholds: p95 latency <= baseline+20ms, error rate delta <= 0.05% absolute; cost-per-token regressions must be < 5% otherwise block.
2026-03-13 - Rollout windows: default business-hours canary for 2 hours, automated ramp over 6 hours if gates pass; out-of-hours full rollout configurable per-customer SLA.
2026-03-13 - Upgrade tooling will be shipped as an opt-in CLI (redwood-upgrade v0) and integrated with Console for one-click guided upgrades for Dedicated/Private customers.

background: Customers deploy across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments and have requested clearer guarantees about which runtime/API/SDK combinations are supported long-term. Current ambiguity increases upgrade friction and operational alerts when rolling changes touch cost/latency. The engineering objective is to reduce upgrade hand-holding and provide automated safe rollouts.
proposed_solution:
1) Produce an authoritative LTS matrix doc that maps: runtime-build-prefix -> API minor versions supported -> SDK minimum/maximum minor versions -> Console version compatibility notes. Represent this as a human-readable doc and machine-parsable manifest (manifest.json maintained in release-infra).
  2) Implement metric-driven rollout gates in release pipeline: automated canaries, synthetic probes, and production shadow checks.
  3) Provide redwood-upgrade CLI to run compatibility checks, perform preflight tests, execute upgrade steps, and trigger rollback hooks.
  4) Expose per-tenant upgrade recommendations in Console with a safe 'Start Upgrade' flow for Dedicated/Private customers.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 0 (analysis): inventory current mappings and customer pins (1 week).
  - Phase 1 (matrix + manifest): publish LTS matrix and manifest in release-infra repo (2 weeks).
  - Phase 2 (automation): build canary pipeline and gates; integrate synthetic tests (3 weeks).
  - Phase 3 (tooling): release redwood-upgrade v0 and Console integration (3 weeks).
  - Phase 4 (pilot): run upgrades for three low-risk Dedicated customers, measure regressions and adjust gates (2 weeks).
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: false-positive gate failures due to noisy metrics. Mitigation: use aggregated baselines and multiple regions; require two consecutive windows to fail before blocking.
  - Risk: customers with strict pinning cannot auto-upgrade. Mitigation: provide a manual, auditable rollback playbook and per-customer maintenance windows via Console.
  - Risk: SDK/runtime mismatch leads to edge-case failures. Mitigation: expand compatibility test harness and add representative integration tests (chat, embeddings, streaming).
